note: Every layer and reading in CAIRN, with the mission, instrument, product and provider it came from.

entries.layer: Terrain elevation (3D surface, slope, routing grid)
entries.product: HiRISE DTM DTEEC_033653_2225_033363_2225_A01 (1 m/post), 'Ice-rich lobate debris apron', Deuteronilus Mensae
entries.provider: HiRISE team, University of Arizona (NASA PDS)
entries.usedFor: 3D terrain mesh (2 m), per-pixel relief lighting (1 m), slope map, metabolic cost of every step, impassable-ground mask, terrain shielding

entries.provider: HiRISE team, University of Arizona (NASA PDS)
entries.usedFor: Ground texture at 25 cm, sand-ripple detection
entries.note: HiRISE is a single-band (grey) image here; the Mars colour in the 3D view is a display tint.

entries.product: The same HiRISE DTM at 20 m and orthoimage ESP_033653_2225_RED_C_01_ORTHO (1 m/px)
entries.provider: HiRISE team, University of Arizona (NASA PDS)
entries.usedFor: Terrain around the walk area in 3D and the regional map in the briefing
entries.note: Outside the HiRISE strip the surroundings are filled with the nearest edge values and fade out.

entries.product: Computed by CAIRN: share of the sky blocked by terrain within 260 m, weighted by a cos² zenith dependence of the surface dose
entries.credit: Derived from NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona data
entries.usedFor: Sky shielding layer, dose along the route, nearest natural cover during the storm
entries.note: Model, not a measurement: the zenith exponent is an assumption.

entries.product: Stops chosen by CAIRN on the HiRISE terrain and imagery (config/stops_deuteronilus.json)
entries.usedFor: Habitat position and science stops: no rover has visited this site
entries.note: Science rationale from the published radar and HiRISE studies of lobate debris aprons; the exact spots are CAIRN's choice.

entries.product: MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0, sols 4189–4194 (18–24 May 2024), detector E dose rate
entries.provider: NASA Planetary Data System, Planetary Plasma Interactions Node
entries.usedFor: Background dose rate and the measured points of the storm replay
entries.note: Measured by Curiosity in Gale Crater, about 6,800 km from this walk area: no instrument has measured radiation in Deuteronilus Mensae. The archive holds 2–4 hours of dosimetry per sol, so the first ~13 hours of the 20 May 2024 storm are filled by a clearly labelled model scaled to NASA's reported 8,100 micrograys.

entries.instrument: DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information)
entries.provider: NASA CCMC / Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office
entries.usedFor: The real eruption record and alert text shown in the storm replay

entries.layer: Exploration Zones on the locator map
entries.mission: NASA Human Exploration of Mars — First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop (2015)
entries.product: Exploration Zone centres (USGS layer 'EZ' on NASA Mars Trek), drawn as 100 km radius circles
entries.provider: NASA Mars Trek (Solar System Treks Project) / USGS Astrogeology
entries.usedFor: Shows where the walk area sits relative to the zones proposed for the first human landings
entries.note: CAIRN's walk area is about 174 km from the centre of the nearer Deuteronilus Mensae zone, i.e. outside it: it was chosen where a HiRISE elevation model exists on the same kind of debris-covered glacier.

entries.product: Mars_Viking_MDIM21_ClrMosaic_global_232m, WMTS tiles at zoom 4 (16° × 9° around the site)
entries.provider: NASA Mars Trek (Solar System Treks Project)
entries.usedFor: The locator inset in the briefing
